name.text: Relationship between elements and sets notation

questiontext.text:
Answer the following questions to get a better understanding of the set theory concept.

1. If \(A\) is a set and \(x\) is an object, how do we use notation to signify whether \(x\) is an element of set \(A\) or not?

a) To show \(x\) is an element of \(A\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

b) To show \(x\) is not an element of \(A\) [[input:ans2]][[validation:ans2]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

2. Consider the sets \(A\) and \(B\):

Set \(A\) contains prime numbers less than \({@selected_number@}\) .

Set \(B\) contains the numbers \(\{{@var_even_set@}\}\).

For each statement below, choose the suitable set notation that correctly describes the given situation involving the sets.

[[input:ans3]][[validation:ans3]][[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

  1. If \(A\) is a set and \(x\) is an object, we use specific notation to show whether \(x\) belongs to \(A\) or not.

    • To show that \(x\) is an element of \(A\), we write

      \(x \in A \)

      The symbol "\(\in \)" means "is an element of."

    • To show that \(x\) is not an element of \(A\), we write

      \(x \notin A \)

      The symbol "\(\notin \)" means "is not an element of."

  2. Consider the sets \(A\) and \(B\). Set \(A\) contains prime numbers less than {@selected_number@} . Set \(B\) contains the numbers \(\{{@var_even_set@}\}\).

    • {@element_to_check@} \( \in A\): This is true, because {@element_to_check@} is a prime number less than {@selected_number@} and therefore it is an element of \(A\).

    • {@element_to_check_1@} \( \notin A\): This is true, because {@element_to_check_1@} is not a prime number and therefore it does not belong to \(A\).

    • \(A \subset B\): This is false, because not all elements of \(A\) (which are primes) are contained in \(B\) (which contains only even numbers).

    • \(B \subset A\): This is false, because no even number greater than 2 is a prime number less than {@selected_number@}.

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

falsefeedback.text: Remember, to express that an object \( x \) is an element of set \( A \), you should use the notation \( x \in A \).
Remember, to express that an object \( x \) is not an element of set \( A \), you should use the notation \( x \notin A \).
